tasks.short: Find candidates for open roles through job boards, agencies, talent pool, referrals and direct outreach.

steps.what: Read vacancy intake and agree channels and must-haves with hiring manager
Post ads on job boards and order flex workers in agency portals
Search talent pool and past applicants for people who fit the must-haves

loop.input: Recruitee talent-pool profiles and CV text plus the vacancy must-haves (certificates, shifts, site, language)
loop.output: Longlist with per-criterion yes/no/unclear and a quoted line from the CV as reason
loop.check: Hard filters (site distance, certificate fields, availability) run as code first; every model claim must cite a CV passage; recruiter reviews every name, nobody is rejected by the score
loop.stop: One pass per profile, max 200 profiles per vacancy; unparseable CVs go to an 'unread' list for the recruiter
loop.why_not_simpler: Experience and certificates sit in free-text CVs, not in structured fields, so keyword search misses most matches

steps.what: Write outreach and referral messages and follow up replies

loop.input: Candidate profile, vacancy text, Recruitee email template
loop.output: Personal outreach draft in Dutch or English placed in Recruitee
loop.check: Template fields filled by code; recruiter edits and approves each send
loop.stop: One draft per candidate, one redraft on request; else recruiter writes it
loop.why_not_simpler: A pure template reads as mass mail and gets low reply rates; the personal line needs the CV

steps.what: Track sources and responses in Excel and report source of hire

tasks.design: Configure Recruitee multiposting, source tags and email templates so ads and tracking stop being manual. A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform reads the Recruitee talent pool via API, applies hard filters in code and runs a bounded model pass that marks must-haves with quoted CV evidence; outreach drafts land in Recruitee for the recruiter to approve. A Power BI page joins Recruitee source tags with AFAS 90-day retention so channels are judged on hires who stay.
tasks.previous_blocker: CVs are free text and the talent pool was unsearchable beyond keywords, and joining Recruitee to AFAS retention needed custom data work nobody had time for.
tasks.enabler_now: Models read CVs reliably enough to cite evidence per criterion, and AI-assisted coding makes the Recruitee and AFAS API jobs a matter of days.
tasks.still_hard: Works council consent and future EU AI Act high-risk duties for any ranking; more AI-written applications lower signal quality; agency portals may lack APIs.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which warehouse team lead will work with which candidate, and the phone call that convinces a passive candidate to come for a shift trial.

ambition.what: Former flex workers and silver-medal applicants in the Recruitee pool get a personal call-back when a matching role opens at their site.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter spends the freed hours on calls and hiring-manager intake instead of posting and copying; they decide which channel mix each site gets based on 90-day retention data.

reach.task: Maintain the Power BI extract joining Recruitee and AFAS
reach.learn: How source-of-hire links to 90-day retention and what data quality it needs
Which roles open each season so sourcing starts before the request

evidence.claim: 91% of hiring leaders use AI; 67% for CV screening, 26% fear missing candidates
Workday agent drafts outreach but sends need recruiter approval
AFAS Profit 8 calculates a match score of applicant to open vacancies
CV screening needs prior works council consent
No rejection based solely on a score under GDPR Art. 22

assumptions: Recruitee API access is included in the current licence
The talent pool holds consented profiles within the retention period
unknowns: How long Noordhaven keeps applicant data and with what consent
Whether the three agency portals offer an API or only screens
Whether AFAS Profit 8 match scoring is licensed or planned
research_questions: How many hires in the last year came from the existing talent pool versus new ads?
Does the model's evidence marking agree with recruiter judgement on 50 past applicants?
Will the OR consent to a ranked-with-reasons longlist with no automatic rejection?

tasks.short: Check selection criteria, tests and interview kits for fairness, job relevance and legal fit; recommend changes.

steps.what: Collect job profiles, ads, interview kits and tests per role
Pull pass rates per stage, site, source and group into Excel
Check criteria against job need, CAO and equal treatment law

loop.input: Ad text, interview kit and job profile for one role, plus a checklist (AWGB grounds, age wording, language demands, certificates the job truly needs)
loop.output: List of flagged criteria with quoted text, checklist item and suggested rewording
loop.check: Each flag must quote the source text and name a checklist item; recruiter accepts or rejects each flag
loop.stop: One pass per document; flags without a quote are dropped; ambiguous cases go to the recruiter as open questions
loop.why_not_simpler: Biased or irrelevant demands hide in wording ('young team', 'native Dutch') that keyword lists miss or over-flag

steps.what: Write recommendation and agree changes with HRBP and hiring managers

loop.output: Short recommendation memo per role family
loop.check: Recruiter edits and signs off before it goes to HRBP
loop.stop: One draft per role family; recruiter rewrites if off
loop.why_not_simpler: The memo argues from mixed numbers and text; a fixed template does not fit each role

tasks.design: A nightly job on the governed data platform pulls Recruitee stage data and SharePoint documents into a Power BI selection-health page with pass rates per stage, site and source. A bounded model pass checks each ad and interview kit against a written checklist and returns quoted flags the recruiter accepts or rejects; accepted flags feed a drafted memo for the HRBP.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stage data lived in Recruitee exports and documents on SharePoint, so a review meant days of manual Excel and reading, done rarely.
tasks.enabler_now: Cheap API pulls and a model that can read wording against a checklist with quotes make a quarterly review a few hours of work.
tasks.still_hard: Dutch employers do not record ethnicity, so group comparisons rely on thin proxies; small volumes per role make pass rates noisy; legal judgement stays with people.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a demand like a forklift certificate or Dutch B1 is truly needed for safety, and persuading a hiring manager to drop a habit.

ambition.what: Review every role family's criteria each quarter instead of only after a complaint or audit.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter becomes the person who signs off selection criteria per role family and brings evidence to hiring managers; the weekly work shifts from compiling to arguing changes.

reach.task: Build the selection-health Power BI page
reach.learn: Which pass-rate gaps are signal and which are small-number noise

reach.task: Maintain mandatory certificate list in Studytube
reach.learn: Which certificates are needed at hire and which can be trained in week one

evidence.claim: Liability for discriminatory selection stays with the employer whatever the vendor contract says
Filtering and evaluating candidates becomes high-risk from 2 December 2027, with logging and oversight duties
Workday generated interview questions for 800+ skills, no evidence of better hires
A model can flag wording against a checklist with quotes

assumptions: Interview kits and job profiles are stored on SharePoint per role
Recruitee stage history is complete enough to compute pass rates
unknowns: Which applicant attributes Noordhaven may lawfully record for fairness monitoring
Whether past complaints or College voor de Rechten van de Mens cases exist
Whether the OR wants to see the review results
research_questions: Do pass rates per stage differ by site or source more than volume noise explains?
How many flags from a test run on 20 current ads does the recruiter accept?
Which criteria do hiring managers refuse to drop, and why?

tasks.short: Plan how to fill current and seasonal staffing needs per site and role.

steps.what: Gather open roles, turnover and seasonal flex demand per site
Analyse time to hire, source yield and 90-day retention per role
Choose channels, flex-to-permanent moves, referral and branding actions
Write plan and present it to HR Director and site managers

loop.input: Dashboard figures and the recruiter's strategy notes
loop.output: Plan document and slide draft per site
loop.check: Numbers inserted by code from the dashboard, not by the model; recruiter edits text
loop.stop: One draft plus one revision; else recruiter writes
loop.why_not_simpler: The narrative differs per site and season; numbers are templated but the argument is not

tasks.design: Replace the Excel sheet that ties AFAS headcount, Recruitee vacancies and agency orders with a nightly job on the governed data platform feeding a Power BI staffing-demand page per site and week. The recruiter decides the strategy; a bounded model step drafts the plan text around figures inserted by code.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agency orders, AFAS headcount and Recruitee lived apart, so demand was rebuilt by hand in Excel once or twice a year.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes the three-source extract and dashboard cheap to build and maintain.
tasks.still_hard: Agency portal data may only come as exports; seasonal peaks depend on customer contracts the HR team does not see early.
tasks.human_edge: Reading site managers and the commercial calendar, and choosing trade-offs between agencies, permanent hires and CAO limits on flex chains.

ambition.what: A monthly per-site hiring plan for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo instead of one yearly plan.

tasks.altitude: The recruiter runs a monthly planning slot with each site and decides which flex roles to convert to permanent; less time compiling numbers.

reach.learn: How the volume forecast drives flex demand and cost
Which turnover risks precede hiring needs

evidence.claim: With process context a hiring agent found stuck candidates and cut time to contract by 27 days
Workday agent flags roles at risk of missing their fill date
Power BI on AFAS extract is already refreshed nightly at Noordhaven

assumptions: The existing nightly AFAS extract can be extended with Recruitee and agency data
Site managers will join a monthly slot
unknowns: What data the three agencies can deliver and in what format
Whether commercial volume forecasts can be shared with HR
research_questions: How far ahead could last year's seasonal peaks have been seen in agency order data?
Does flex-to-permanent conversion show better 90-day retention than outside hires?
Would site managers act on a monthly plan?

tasks.short: Build, schedule, run and score applicant tests such as forklift practicals and reading tests; check they work.

steps.what: Build or update test questions and practical checklists

loop.input: Job profile, safety instructions, required certificate content
loop.output: Draft question bank and practical checklist with answer keys
loop.check: Recruiter and site safety lead review every item before use; no personality or emotion inference items
loop.stop: One draft per test version; rejected items rewritten by the recruiter
loop.why_not_simpler: Questions must reflect each site's actual work instructions written in free text

steps.what: Schedule tests and invite candidates by mail
Run the test on site or online with the candidate
Score results and record them in Recruitee
Check test pass rates against 90-day retention and group gaps

tasks.design: Configure Recruitee self-scheduling and templates for test invites; a tablet form (Microsoft Forms or a small Power App) scores multiple-choice and practical checklists by code and writes the result into Recruitee for recruiter sign-off. A Power BI page links test results to AFAS 90-day retention; a bounded model step only drafts new question items for human review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tests ran on paper per site, so scores never reached a system and nobody could check whether tests predicted who stayed.
tasks.enabler_now: Low-code forms and the Recruitee API are quick to wire with AI-assisted coding; question drafting is cheap.
tasks.still_hard: Small numbers per test version make validity checks weak; tests that decide on candidates fall under GDPR Art. 22 and later the AI Act high-risk regime.
tasks.human_edge: Watching a candidate drive a reach truck safely and judging nerves versus lack of skill; deciding pass or fail stays with a person.

ambition.what: A yearly test validity report per site showing which tests predict 90-day retention.

tasks.altitude: Scheduling and paperwork drop out; the recruiter owns test design per role family with evidence of what predicts staying.

reach.task: Forklift and VCA certification in Studytube
reach.learn: Where test content overlaps with onboarding training
How to read validity numbers on small samples

evidence.claim: Emotion inference in hiring is banned under AI Act Art. 5(1)(f)
Review must be meaningful, not rubber-stamping an automated score
Scheduling is among the most common AI uses in hiring (59%)

assumptions: Practical tests are run by the recruiter or a site trainer on site
Recruitee scheduling is in the current licence
unknowns: Which tests are in use per site and who administers them
Whether test results are kept and for how long
Whether the OR has agreed on applicant testing
research_questions: Do current forklift or reading test scores relate to 90-day retention?
How many recruiter hours per month go to scheduling tests today?
Will site trainers use a tablet form on the warehouse floor?

role.altitude: The two recruiters move from posting, copying and scheduling to intake, candidate calls and owning the evidence on which channels, criteria and tests produce hires still there at day 90. They gain sign-off on selection criteria per role family and a monthly hiring plan per site.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: the Recruitee-AFAS join behind source and test validity
HR Business Partner: site workforce planning and flex-to-permanent conversion
Learning and Development Specialist: which certificates to require at hire versus train in week one
skills_to_grow: Reading funnel and retention data on small samples
Writing and testing selection checklists against Dutch equal treatment law
Overseeing AI drafts and ranked lists under GDPR Art. 22 and the AI Act
Running monthly planning with site managers
role.ambitious_version: Recruitee, AFAS and agency data are joined nightly; every role family has reviewed criteria and tests linked to 90-day retention, flex workers and past applicants are called back first, and each site gets a monthly hiring plan, all with OR consent and AI Act oversight in place before December 2027.
